Understanding the Assignment

Dr. Benson Kiarie, PhDLead Evaluator | CEO, Vantage Africa

About the Congregation

The Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd runs community-based missions in South Africa that serve women, girls, children and others living in poverty and vulnerability. Its work is delivered through three mission sites: Hebron and Madidi in North West Province and Akhanani in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape.

The Strategic Plan 2022–2026, informed by a 2021 Community Needs Assessment, commits the Congregation to four objectives, shown below.

What the Congregation needs

An independent, participatory and safeguarding-sensitive evaluation that shows what the Strategic Plan achieved, what helped or hindered it, how sustainable the results are, and what the next strategic cycle should prioritise.

Why this evaluation matters now

As the 2022–2026 cycle ends, the Congregation must decide what to continue, strengthen or change. A credible evaluation gives the Sisters, Partners-in-Mission and funders such as GSIF evidence of results across the three sites, an honest account of challenges and enabling factors, and prioritised recommendations that can feed directly into the next strategic plan. The ToR asks for an assessment against the OECD-DAC criteria, with full participation of communities and strict safeguarding of children and adults at risk; it does not include writing a new plan.

2

Our Evaluation Approach

We will conduct a theory-based, participatory evaluation that tests the Strategic Plan’s Theory of Change against what actually happened at Hebron, Madidi and Akhanani. Evidence from documents and monitoring data will be combined with the voices of Sisters, staff, partners, programme participants and community members, so that every conclusion rests on more than one source. The approach applies the five OECD-DAC criteria named in the ToR, adapted to the evidence available.

The Five OECD-DAC Criteria

1

Relevance

Did the Strategic Plan stay relevant to community needs and the South African context?

Needs Assessment 2021; community FGDs; KIIs

2

Effectiveness

To what extent were the objectives, initiatives and intended results achieved?

Monitoring data; programme reports; KIIs

3

Efficiency

Were resources, people and partnerships used well to deliver results?

Reports; budgets; staff interviews

4

Impact / Contribution

What significant changes did the Plan contribute to for women, girls and children?

Most Significant Change stories; FGDs

5

Sustainability

Will results and capacities last beyond 2026?

Leadership and partner KIIs; capacity review

Three Principles That Guide the Evaluation

1

Participatory

Sisters, Partners-in-Mission, staff, programme participants and community members all shape the findings.

2

Safe and ethical

Informed consent, confidentiality, trauma-informed interviewing and referral pathways for anyone at risk.

3

Utilisation-focused

Every finding leads to a practical, prioritised recommendation for the next strategic cycle.

Evaluation Matrix and Safeguarding

The matrix links each of the six specific objectives in the ToR to the questions we will answer, the evidence we will look for and where it will come from. Findings will be rated objective by objective so the Congregation can see clearly what was achieved, partly achieved or not achieved.

ToR objectiveKey evaluation questionWhat we will look atMain sources
1. Achievement of objectivesTo what extent were the objectives, initiatives and intended results achieved?Targets vs. results for each of the four objectivesMonitoring data; reports; KIIs
2. RelevanceDid the Plan remain relevant to community needs and context?Fit with 2021 Needs Assessment; participant viewsNeeds Assessment; FGDs
3. Enabling and constraining factorsWhat internal and external factors helped or hindered implementation?Factors cited by stakeholders; context changesKIIs; document review
4. Sustainability and capacityHow sustainable are results and the capacities built?Capacity of Sisters and Partners; continuity of servicesKIIs; capacity review
5. Lessons and good practiceWhat worked well and what should change?Documented practices and lessonsFGDs; MSC stories; validation
6. RecommendationsWhat should inform future programming and strategy?Prioritised, costed-in-principle actionsAnalysis; validation session

Safeguarding and Ethics

1

Written or verbal informed consent from every participant

2

No interviews with children without a guardian and a safeguarding focal person present

3

Trauma-informed questions for GBV-related discussions; no probing of individual cases

4

Referral to the Congregation’s counselling and safe-space services if distress arises

5

Anonymised notes; data stored securely and deleted after the assignment

6

Compliance with the Congregation’s safeguarding policy and code of conduct

From Data to Findings

Collect

Documents, monitoring data, KIIs, FGDs, MSC stories

Code

By objective and OECD-DAC criterion

Triangulate

Across sources, sites and stakeholder groups

Rate

Achieved, partly achieved, not achieved

Present

Scorecards, charts and clear narrative

What We Will Ask for Each Strategic Objective

Detailed questions to be refined with the Congregation during inception

The ToR’s overarching questions will be applied to each of the four objectives, so that leadership receives a clear verdict on every part of the Strategic Plan. For each objective we will rate achievement as achieved, partly achieved or not achieved, explain why, and recommend what to continue, adapt or stop.

Objective 1

Reduce Poverty

Education, skills development and job opportunities

  • How many women, girls and youth completed education and skills programmes, against Plan targets?
  • Did participants gain employment, start income activities or continue in education?
  • Which skills and pathways led most often to real income?

Evidence:Enrolment and completion; employment and income outcomes; participant stories

Objective 2

Reduce Hunger

Sustainable nutrition programmes

  • Did households reached by nutrition programmes eat more regularly and more nutritiously?
  • Are food gardens and nutrition activities still running without direct support?
  • Who was reached, and who was missed?

Evidence:People reached; food security changes; continuity of gardens and feeding

Objective 3

End GBV and Safeguard

Advocacy, counselling, education and safe spaces

  • Were survivors and people at risk able to access counselling and safe spaces when needed?
  • Did awareness and advocacy shift attitudes or reporting in the communities?
  • How well did referral and safeguarding systems work in practice?

Evidence:Service use; referral functioning; community perceptions (no individual case probing)

Objective 4

Strengthen Capacity

Sisters and Partners-in-Mission

  • What skills, systems and partnerships were strengthened between 2022 and 2026?
  • Is monitoring data good enough to guide the next strategy?
  • Which capacities are still needed to sustain impact?

Evidence:Capacity review; quality of monitoring data; partnerships and funding base

Achieved

Targets met or exceeded, with credible evidence

Partly achieved

Clear progress, but gaps in reach, quality or evidence

Not achieved

Little progress, or no reliable evidence of results
